extracted.intended_audience: OSHA stakeholders and public commenters (employers, workers, labor organizations, researchers, state planners)
extracted.subtask_description: Search results and summaries related to Federal Register documents on heat injury and illness prevention, useful for drafting notice-and-comment submissions on OSHA rulemaking and related federal/state actions. Includes definitions, proposed employer obligations, program elements, and notices soliciting data or stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability of OSHA heat prevention standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed standard would apply to all employers conducting outdoor and indoor work in all general industry, construction, maritime, and agriculture sectors where OSHA has jurisdiction, with some exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a programmatic standard that would clarify employer obligations and the steps necessary to effectively protect employees from hazardous heat. Multiple notices reiterate the broad sectoral coverage and that OSHA seeks input on the scope of the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer requirement to create a heat-hazard plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard would require employers to create a plan to evaluate and control heat hazards in their workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterized as a programmatic element; plan should evaluate sources of heat (e.g., metabolic heat and the environment) and retention (e.g., clothing/PPE), and implement controls. OSHA requests comments and data on the elements such a plan should include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rest breaks to prevent heat illness
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule and accompanying summaries state employers would be required to implement rest breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rest breaks are repeatedly listed among core employer obligations alongside shade, water, training, and response planning. Notices extending comment periods and stakeholder meetings reference rest-break requirements as a key element for public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to shade and water
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers would be required to provide access to shade and water for employees exposed to hazardous heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in Federal Register summaries and Presidential statements as a fundamental protective measure, typically paired with rest breaks and response procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for employees and supervisors
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule would require training employees and supervisors about heat hazards and prevention measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is indicated as part of employer obligations to prevent heat illness and is repeatedly mentioned in summaries of the proposed rule and related outreach materials (stakeholder meetings, NACOSH discussions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat illness response planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers would be required to develop a plan to respond to heat illness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response planning appears as a discrete requirement (e.g., for handling heat exhaustion or heat stroke) and is listed with other program elements; public comments and hearing materials are solicited on the content and implementation of such plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: heat stress, heat strain, heat-related illness, heat-related injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat stress: the combined load of heat a person experiences from sources of heat (i.e., metabolic heat and the environment) and heat retention (e.g., from clothing or personal protective equipment). Heat strain: the body's response to heat stress (ACGIH, 2023). Heat-related illness: adverse clinical health outcomes that occur due to heat exposure, such as heat exhaustion or heat stroke. Heat-related injury: an injury linked to heat exposure that is not a typical symptom of heat-related illness (e.g., a fall or cut).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are used throughout the NPRM and ANPRM to frame scope, measurement, and the types of outcomes the standard is intended to prevent; references include ACGIH terminology and are cited across documents in the search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program elements and amenities for worker housing and projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for certain housing programs are encouraged to include amenities in projects that help prevent heat illness or promote recovery from potential impacts of heat exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: RHS notice for Off-Farm Labor Housing encourages inclusion of design/features to protect outdoor workers from heat illness. This indicates funding/program guidance that considers heat-illness prevention as a criterion for project planning/selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan adoption and equivalency for heat-illness standards
rubrics_metrics.description: State occupational safety and health plans may adopt heat illness prevention standards; OSHA can approve state-initiated changes (example: Oregon's OARs establishing new Heat Illness Prevention standards for general industry and agricultural workers and amendments to labor housing standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices document the process and that OSHA found state rules to be at least as effective as Federal standards when approving them under Section 18(e). State-level standards (with citations to specific OARs) serve as models and raise questions about equivalency and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and evidence on heat impacts (including cognitive effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: CDC and other agencies invited comments or proposed data collection projects designed to evaluate and assess the cognitive impacts of heat exposure on workers and gather information on prevalence/incidence, reporting of severe symptoms to employers, and heat-stress interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices under the Paperwork Reduction Act solicit public input on proposed surveys and information collections; these data are intended to inform rulemaking and guidance by quantifying burden, incidence, and effectiveness of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NACOSH Heat Injury and Illness Prevention Work Group responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The NACOSH Heat Injury and Illness Prevention Work Group will evaluate OSHA's heat illness and prevention guidance materials, develop recommendations for guidance materials, evaluate stakeholder input, and develop recommendations on potential elements of a proposed heat injury and illness prevention standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work group activities include public meetings (WebEx), developing written findings, and presenting recommendations to the full NACOSH committee; notices set meeting dates and solicit participation/registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and reporting considerations related to injuries and illnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA's recordkeeping amendments (broader rule) require certain employers to electronically submit injury and illness information (OSHA Forms 300/301/300A) and related decisions about public posting and identification removal — relevant to tracking heat-related illnesses/injuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not heat-specific, these recordkeeping requirements affect how heat-related cases would be documented and reported to OSHA; summaries note restrictions on personal identifiers and planned public posting of de-identified data.
